clue.text: Appropriate power unit for spinning-jenny?

parts.note: a jenny is also a female donkey, so the fitting motor for a spinning-jenny would be one named after that animal

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what motor best suits an old cotton-spinning machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The spinning-jenny was an early multi-spindle spinning machine; the joke rests on 'jenny' as a female ass, and a small auxiliary steam engine on ships bears the animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small auxiliary steam engine, used for hoisting on ships and docks.

clue.text: County girl socially accepted at the outset

parts.note: the done thing is what is socially accepted; 'at the outset' places this piece first
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl from some county is welcomed into society from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outset' puts the second-named piece first. Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is an Irish county in the province of Ulster.

clue.text: Like a certain element in tours, disorderly

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of order, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some element behaves chaotically while out on tours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' rearranges the seven letters of IN TOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrous describes compounds of nitrogen, a chemical element.

clue.text: Quarters fitted like an open prison?

parts.note: E (east) is one of the compass quarters
S (south) is another compass quarter
fitted for a job means capable of it

explanation.surface: Lodgings furnished in the style of a low-security jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' gives two compass points, E and S, rather than lodgings. The question mark flags that an open prison is merely one that can be got out of.
explanation.definitionFit: An open prison has few barriers, so leaving it is possible, which is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Distinctive character in Macbeth ostentatiously presented

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A play's grandstanding performance gives it its special quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across macbETH OStentatiously; 'presented' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos means the characteristic spirit or values of a person, group or culture.

clue.text: Yellow wild birds found around marsh

indicators.note: the birds are placed around the marsh, enclosing it

parts.note: game is wild birds hunted for sport
a bog is a marsh

explanation.surface: Wild yellow birds turn up near a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild birds' is one piece, the game shot for sport, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a gum resin used as a deep yellow pigment, and by extension that colour.

clue.text: This blissful state will be the end of me!

definitions.text: This blissful state will be the end of me!

parts.words: This blissful state will be the end of me!
parts.note: in Buddhism the blissful goal is reached by the extinction of the self, so it literally ends the 'me'

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that pure happiness will finish them off.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation sounds like a throwaway remark, but in Buddhist teaching this state really is the extinguishing of individual self and desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect peace in which the individual self is extinguished.

clue.text: Undress uniform worn some officers?

parts.note: detectives wear ordinary civilian dress rather than uniform, which is a sort of uniform of their own

explanation.surface: Informal kit is what certain officers wear on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undress' in military usage means ordinary or informal dress, not nakedness; the clue as printed appears to lack 'by' after 'worn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives on duty wear ordinary civilian dress, so they are said to be in this.

clue.text: Crackpot I mostly call "nut'?

indicators.note: crackpot suggests something crazy and broken, so the letters that follow are scrambled
most of the word call is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone eccentric admits they usually describe themselves as nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CALL to CAL; 'Crackpot' then rearranges I + CAL + NUT, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot or nut is a mad or eccentric person, as the word for a madman implies.

clue.text: Decomposed matter around king's bone

indicators.note: the rotted matter is placed around the king, enclosing him

parts.note: humus is decomposed organic matter in soil
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A monarch's skeleton is found surrounded by rotting soil.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Latin rex, king) is a crossword convention; 'Decomposed' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition of the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm.

clue.text: Big hitter finds one pretending to protect line on boundary

indicators.note: the pretender is wrapped around the other pieces, guarding them

parts.note: a shammer is someone who shams or pretends

indicators.note: the line comes on top of, ahead of, the boundary

parts.note: an edge is a boundary

explanation.surface: A powerful batsman fakes it while guarding the line at the rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (big hitter, boundary) misleads: the hitter is a heavy hammer, and 'to protect' wraps the pretender around the line and boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledgehammer is a large heavy hammer swung with both hands, a literal big hitter.

clue.text: Breaking up old ring, an exclusive clique

indicators.note: breaking the pieces apart lets their letters be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old gang splits up, though it was a select little circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges UP + O + RING.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-group is a small exclusive circle of people sharing interests, who keep outsiders out.

clue.text: Son has to carry on packing cargo

parts.note: to wage a war or campaign is to carry it on

explanation.surface: A boy must keep going while loading a ship's freight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry on' means wage, as in carrying on a campaign, not continuing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowage is the stacking and packing of goods in a hold.

clue.text: Head off rows of inferior animals

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is taken away

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat, so sculls means rows

explanation.surface: A command to intercept lines of second-rate livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' is the verb (as in rowing a boat), giving SCULLS, which loses its head S.
explanation.definitionFit: Culls are animals weeded out of a herd or flock as substandard.

clue.text: Homing missile

parts.note: not a guided weapon but a thrown stick that comes back home to the thrower

explanation.surface: A guided weapon that locks on to its target.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a modern guided rocket; here 'homing' means returning to where it started.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is a curved throwing stick designed to return to the thrower.

clue.text: Not engaged, having no up-to-date clothes

definitions.meaning: of machinery, disconnected from the drive, in neutral
gear means clothing, so being out of the fashionable gear

explanation.surface: Someone single and badly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A car in neutral has its drive disconnected; read literally, the phrase also means lacking trendy clothing.

clue.text: Stayed out too late

parts.note: not a late night on the town but remaining asleep, out cold, past the time to get up

explanation.surface: A reveller came home far past curfew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stayed out' suggests partying; it means unconscious in sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep beyond the intended waking time is what the clue's reading describes.

clue.text: Major selling points of opera I'm composing

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: The big attractions of an opera I'm writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composing' rearranges OPERA I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, plural of emporium, are large stores or trading centres.

clue.text: Hide contents?' Enough : to make one drunk

definitions.meaning: a skin is a hide, so its contents would be as much as it holds
a quantity of alcohol sufficient to intoxicate

explanation.surface: What a hide holds is enough to get one sozzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the word means as much drink as a person can take, enough to make them drunk.

clue.text: In a church it is' commonly dropped

definitions.text: In a church it is' commonly dropped

indicators.note: the word it is placed inside the other pieces

explanation.surface: Something in church is habitually let fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the name of the letter H, commonly dropped in casual speech ('ouse for house).
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the letter H, often left unpronounced in Cockney and other accents.

clue.text: Find fault with a sound rule

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sound signals that the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: A complaint about a well-founded regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable; it signals that 'a reign' is said aloud, matching the answer in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to accuse or censure, finding fault formally.

clue.text: Part of a service where refilling may be required

definitions.text: Part of a service where refilling may be required

parts.words: Part of a service where refilling may be required
parts.note: not a petrol station but a tea set, whose cups need topping up

explanation.surface: Motorway services where you must fill up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a garage or service station; it is a tea service.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacups form part of a tea service and are refilled with tea.

clue.text: Bound to join up with, say, light infantryman

parts.note: to bound is to hop or leap
lite is an informal or commercial spelling of light, which 'say' hints at

explanation.surface: An infantryman is bound to team up with something light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks LITE as a variant spelling of light. A hoplite was a heavily armed foot soldier of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoplite was a heavily armed foot soldier in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Invest — you'll find both value and revenue do

parts.words: you'll find both value and revenue do
parts.note: both words finish with the same two letters

explanation.surface: Investing pays off, as value and revenue both show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' means endow or clothe; the rest is a cryptic hint, since valUE and revenUE both end in the letters U and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or invest someone with a quality.

clue.text: Prepare for "trouble, taking member's part

definitions.meaning: to arm oneself in advance against something
a limb is a member, and this is a section of the arm

explanation.surface: Get ready for strife by taking a piece of a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm beforehand is to get ready for trouble; it is also the arm between elbow and wrist.

clue.text: Carried out air attacks limited defence skills repelled

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the combined pieces are read in reverse
limited means cut short, so only the start of defence is kept

parts.note: arts are skills

explanation.surface: Air raids were launched because the defensive abilities were poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' cuts DEFENCE to DEF; with ARTS that makes DEFARTS, and 'repelled' turns the whole run to STRAFED.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Mince pie with preserve for gourmet

indicators.note: mince means chop up, so the letters of pie are rearranged

parts.note: to cure food is to preserve it by salting or smoking

explanation.surface: A mince pie with jam for someone with refined tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pie' reads as the Christmas pastry; 'Mince' is the anagram signal for PIE, giving EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person devoted to fine food and drink, a connoisseur.

clue.text: Dance directions designed to make turns easier

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
bearings are compass directions

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dance help one turn more smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance directions' suggests steps for dancing; it is BALL then BEARINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small steel spheres in a race that reduce friction in rotating machine parts.
